Function Details

createArea(subtype, name, nodes=None, edges=None)

 

Convenience function to create an area.

The end-point nodes for edges are inferred and do not need to be contained in nodes as well.

Parameters:
  • subtype (str) - The usertype of the area to be created.
  • name (str) - The name of the area to be created.
  • nodes (Iterable(INode) | none) - The collection of (isolated) nodes. None means the empty set, which is the default to nodes.
  • edges (Iterable(IEdge) | none) - The collection of edges. None means the empty set. End-points of edges do not need to be members in nodes; they are inferred.
Returns: IGraph
The created area.
Decorators:
  • @typedoc

generateArea(subtype, name, graph, delimUserTypes, nodes=None, edges=None, isDelimiting=None)

 

Iteratively enlarge area implicitly defined by the nodes and edges.

The area is enlarged edge by edge, skipping the edges that have a start node containing an object of any user type listed in delimUserTypes.

Note that it is not necessary that nodes belonging to edges in edges are members of nodes; those that are missing are automatically added.

Parameters:
  • subtype (str) - The usertype of the area to be enlarged.
  • name (str) - The name of the area to be enlarged.
  • graph (IGraph) - The traversal graph containing the nodes and edges.
  • delimUserTypes (Iterable(str)) - The user types that halt enlargement from the node. If a node contains an object of any user type in delimUserTypes, no enlargement will continue from that node.
  • nodes (Iterable(INode) | none) - The start collection of nodes. None means the empty set.
  • edges (Iterable(IEdge) | none) - The start collection of edges. None means the empty set. End points of edges do not need to be members in nodes; they are inferred.
  • isDelimiting (function | none) - Callback that maps (railyard object, index) to bool. Should return True if the given object having user type in c{delimUserTypes} should delimit the area assuming it is approached from the given index.
Returns: IGraph
The maximally enlarged area generated from the given "sub-area".
Decorators:
  • @typedoc

connectedComponentsOfArea(area, pathComponents=True)

 

Return a list of connected components in the considered area.

Each of the components is an area separating from others and containing either a single node or a set of connected edges belonging to area.

Parameters:
  • area (IGraph) - The area from which connected components are derived.
  • pathComponents (bool) - If true, two edges are connected iff there is a standard traversal relation defined on them. For example, straight leg and bent leg of a standard are not considered as connected if pathComponents is true.
Returns: [IGraph]
A list of connected area components of area.
Decorators:
  • @typedoc

connectedComponents(railyard, pathComponents=True)

 

Return a list of connected components in the railyard.

Each of the components is an area separating from others and containing either a single node or a set of connected edges belonging to railyard.

Parameters:
  • railyard (IRailyard) - The railyard from which connected components are derived.
  • pathComponents (bool) - If true, two edges are connected iff there is a standard traversal relation defined on them. For example, straight leg and bent leg of a standard are not considered as connected if pathComponents is true.
Returns: [IGraph]
A list of connected area components of c{railyard}.
